mainTopic: How different תנאים learn rules about בכור and מעשר שני from one פסוק, the end of פרק אלו קדשים, and the opening משנה about חטאות that are left to die.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא in which several תנאים each learn something different from one פסוק. That פסוק (דברים 14:23) lists מעשר שני right next to בכור. First, רבי ישמעאל learns מעשר שני from בכור. The גמרא asks whether this breaks רבי יוחנן's rule against לָמֵד מִן הַלָּמֵד in קדשים, and answers that מעשר is חולין and that the meat and blood of a בכור count as one thing. רבי עקיבא learns that a בכור may be brought up only from where מעשר דגן is brought, meaning ארץ ישראל. בן עזאי learns that מעשר שני is eaten only inside the walls of ירושלים, and the גמרא explains that the idea of eating it anywhere within sight came from the rule in שילה. אחרים use the היקש to teach that a בכור does not become פסול when its year passes. The גמרא then shows where each side gets the rules the other side learns: 'שנה בשנה' and 'כחזה התנופה' cover not becoming פסול after a year and eating for two days and one night. The פרק ends with a הדרן, and a new משנה opens listing חטאות that are left to die.

steps.title: Second tithe is learned from the firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes רבי ישמעאל's comparison: מעשר שני learns its rule from בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And then מעשר comes and learns from בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the chain of learning it started before: מעשר שני takes its rule from בכור. This line also sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the meat of a בכור was tied to its blood, so it can only be eaten when the blood can be put on the מזבח. Now מעשר שני, which the פסוק places right next to בכור, takes that same rule. That makes it a two-step chain, which is exactly what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe: produce brought to ירושלים and eaten there
A firstborn male kosher animal, which is holy and given to a כהן
And it learns (its law) from
Learning one law from another because the פסוק places them side by side

phrases.english: And then מעשר comes
phrases.notes: This means מעשר שני, which the פסוק mentions right next to בכור.

phrases.english: and learns from בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, מעשר שני takes its law from בכור, so it is eaten in ירושלים only when the blood of a בכור could be put on the מזבח.

steps.title: Can holy things be learned in a two-step chain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this using רבי יוחנן's rule that in קדשים we do not learn from something that was itself learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can we learn holy things from each other? Didn't רבי יוחנן say: in the whole Torah we may learn a law from a law that was itself learned, except for קדשים, where we may not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the chain from Step 1. It quotes רבי יוחנן, who says that for holy things you cannot learn a second step from something that was already learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat of a בכור got its rule from its blood, so that rule is already 'learned.' Then מעשר learns from the meat, which is a second step. רבי יוחנן says this kind of chain is not allowed for קדשים, so the derivation seems to break.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a law from another law that was itself learned from somewhere else
Holy items, especially קרבנות
From one another
But didn't he say? (opens a challenge from a known statement)

steps.confusionAlert: The rule is not that קדשים can never be learned from something. The problem is only learning in a second step, from a law that was itself learned.

phrases.english: And do we learn holy things from one another?
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
In the entire Torah,
we learn something learned from something that was itself learned,
except for holy things,
where we do not learn something learned from something that was itself learned!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי יָלְפִינַן בְּקָדָשִׁים מֵהֲדָדֵי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation stated in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The chain blood of בכור → meat of בכור → מעשר שני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is a two-step learning chain in קדשים, which רבי יוחנן forbids.

steps.title: Second tithe counts as non-holy
steps.stepSummary: Answer: מעשר שני is חולין, so the special rule for קדשים does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעשר is חולין (not holy in the קרבן sense).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the thing being learned, מעשר שני, is not קדשים at all. It is חולין, so רבי יוחנן's rule does not stop it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's limit applies only when the thing being learned is a holy item. Since מעשר is counted as חולין, the normal Torah-wide rule applies, and a two-step chain is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-holy, ordinary items (not קרבנות)
מעשר is counted as non-holy
Holy item, the opposite of חולין

phrases.english: מעשר is non-holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the category of the learned item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought מעשר shares the special rule for קדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר is חולין, so two-step learning is allowed for it.

steps.title: What if we look at the source instead?
steps.stepSummary: The answer works only if we judge by the item being learned. If we judge by the source doing the teaching (the meat of a בכור, which is holy), there is still a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says we follow the item being learned. But for the one who says we follow the item doing the teaching, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 3. The answer 'מעשר is חולין' works for only one of two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a disagreement about which side decides whether the קדשים rule applies. One view looks at the item being learned (מעשר, which is חולין). The other looks at the source doing the teaching (the meat of a בכור, which is holy and itself learned from the blood). By the second view, the problem from Step 2 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one view, but...)
We follow the item being learned
We follow the source doing the teaching
What is there to say? (the answer seems not to work)

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
we follow the item being learned,
but according to the one who says
we follow the item doing the teaching,
phrases.notes: Here the teacher is the meat of the בכור, which is holy and already learned its rule from the blood.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בָּתַר לָמֵד אָזְלִינַן, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בָּתַר מְלַמֵּד אָזְלִינַן, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of Step 3 to one opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that מעשר is חולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the source decides, the source is holy and already learned, so רבי יוחנן's rule still blocks the chain.

steps.title: Meat and blood are one thing
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the meat and blood of a בכור count as one item, so there is really only one step of learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meat and blood are one matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the blood and meat of the בכור are not two separate items. So the meat did not 'learn' from the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If meat and blood are one unit, the rule about the meat is not a learned rule. It is part of one rule about the בכור. Then מעשר learns directly from the בכור in a single step, which is allowed even by the view that follows the teaching source.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat
Blood
One single matter

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל's comparison of מעשר שני to בכור survives both ways of looking at it. מעשר is חולין, and the meat and blood of a בכור count as one item, so there is no forbidden two-step chain.

phrases.english: Meat and blood
are one matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The meat of a בכור learned its rule from the blood, making a two-step chain.
steps.terutzMaskana: Meat and blood are one unit, so the learning is a single step.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks about a firstborn from outside the Land
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא raises the possibility that a בכור from חוץ לארץ could be brought to ארץ ישראל and offered when the בית המקדש stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: I might think a person may bring a בכור from outside the Land to the Land when the בית המקדש is standing, and offer it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to רבי עקיבא's view. He opens with a 'you might think' line, which sets up the proof from the פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יכול brings up an idea only so it can be rejected. The question is whether a בכור born outside ארץ ישראל can still become a קרבן if someone brings it to the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (an idea raised in order to reject it)
Outside ארץ ישראל
The Temple is standing
And offer it as a קרבן

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
One might think a person may bring up a firstborn
from outside the Land to the Land
when the Temple is standing
and offer it?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל יַעֲלֶה אָדָם בְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי ישמעאל's use of the פסוק to רבי עקיבא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the question of whether a בכור from חוץ לארץ may be offered.

steps.title: The verse links firstborn to grain tithe
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק places בכור next to מעשר דגן, so a בכור is brought up from the same place that מעשר דגן is brought up from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall eat before ה' your God the tithe of your grain, your wine and your oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and your flock.' From the place you bring up grain tithe, you bring up a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers his own question with a פסוק that mentions מעשר דגן and בכור together. He says the two follow the same rule about where they may be brought from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same פסוק רבי ישמעאל used, but רבי עקיבא learns something different from it. Since מעשר דגן is only brought from ארץ ישראל, a בכור may also only be brought from there.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (introduces the proof verse)
The tithe of grain
Bring up (to ירושלים)

phrases.english: The verse states:
“And you shall eat before the Lord your God
the tithe of your grain, your wine, and your oil,
and the firstborn of your cattle and your flock” —
from the place that you bring up grain tithe,
you bring up a firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְאָכַלְתָּ לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the יכול of Step 6 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: Where a בכור may be brought from
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 14:23, where בכור is placed next to מעשר דגן

steps.title: No firstborn from where grain tithe is not brought
steps.stepSummary: The flip side: from a place where מעשר דגן is not brought up (חוץ לארץ), a בכור is not brought up either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from a place that you do not bring up grain tithe, you do not bring up a בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא states the conclusion: a בכור from outside ארץ ישראל may not be brought and offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר דגן applies only in ארץ ישראל, so by the link in the פסוק a בכור from חוץ לארץ cannot be offered. This answers the יכול from Step 6 with a clear 'no,' and it differs from רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: You do not bring up
From the place
From the positive statement you can hear the negative one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: a בכור may be offered only if it comes from ארץ ישראל, the same place מעשר דגן is brought from.
steps.whyThisMatters: This view explains why a בכור from חוץ לארץ might not be accepted as a קרבן, while רבי ישמעאל's view allows it.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִמְּקוֹם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה מַעֲלֶה מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן —
phrases.english: And from a place that you do not bring up grain tithe —
phrases.notes: This means חוץ לארץ, where מעשר דגן does not apply.

phrases.english: you do not bring up a firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמְּקוֹם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה מַעֲלֶה מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן אִי אַתָּה מַעֲלֶה בְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the negative side of the proof in Step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי עקיבא, a בכור from חוץ לארץ may not be brought to the בית המקדש and offered.

steps.title: בן עזאי's opening question about מעשר שני
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי raises the idea that מעשר שני might be eaten anywhere within sight of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי says: You might think a person can bring up מעשר שני and eat it in any place from which ירושלים can be seen.
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי opens a new teaching with a "you might think" idea. He is setting up the question he will answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יכול brings up a possible mistake so it can be ruled out. The question is not whether מעשר שני must be brought to ירושלים. It is how far its eating area reaches: only inside the walls, or anywhere the city can be seen from.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe: produce that must be brought to ירושלים and eaten there
"You might think": brings up a possible mistake so it can be rejected
Anywhere from which the holy place can be seen

phrases.english: Ben Azzai says:
You might think a person may bring up second tithe,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and eat it in any place that sees [the city]?
phrases.notes: He means any spot outside the walls from which you can still see ירושלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching in the ברייתא, this time about מעשר שני instead of בכור from חוץ לארץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Raises the possibility that מעשר שני may be eaten anywhere within sight of ירושלים.

steps.title: A logical comparison to firstborn
steps.stepSummary: Both בכור and מעשר שני must be brought to the holy place. Since בכור is eaten only inside the walls, מעשר שני should be the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: We could learn this by logic: a בכור must be brought to the chosen place, and מעשר must be brought to the chosen place. Just as a בכור is eaten only inside the walls, מעשר should also be eaten only inside the walls.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tries to answer the "you might think" with a logical comparison to בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both items share one feature: each must be brought to ירושלים. Based on that shared feature, the rule of בכור (eaten only inside the walls) is carried over to מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is a logical argument": we could learn this by reasoning
Bringing to the chosen place (ירושלים)
Inside the city walls

phrases.english: But it is a logical inference:
a firstborn requires being brought to the place,
and tithe requires being brought to the place —

phrases.aramaic: מָה בְּכוֹר אֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל אֶלָּא לִפְנִים מִן הַחוֹמָה,
phrases.english: just as a firstborn is eaten only within the wall,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַעֲשֵׂר אֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל אֶלָּא לִפְנִים מִן הַחוֹמָה.
phrases.english: so too tithe is eaten only within the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the "you might think" of step 9 using logic.
steps.raayaObject: That מעשר שני is eaten only inside the walls
steps.raayaSupportSource: A logical comparison to בכור, which also must be brought to the chosen place

steps.title: Firstborn is stricter, so the comparison fails
steps.stepSummary: The logic is pushed away: a בכור goes on the מזבח, which makes it stricter than מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a בכור? It is special because its blood and fats are put on the מזבח. Can you say the same about מעשר, which has none of that?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the logical comparison it just made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור has a stricter side that מעשר שני lacks: its blood and fats go on the מזבח. Because בכור is more holy in this way, its strict eating rule may not carry over to the less strict מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: "What about X, since it has...": pointing out a strict feature that breaks a comparison
Putting the blood on the מזבח
The fats and parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: What about a firstborn?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן טָעוּן מַתַּן דָּמִים וְאֵימוּרִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: It is special in that it requires placing blood and sacrificial parts on the altar;
will you say the same about tithe, which does not?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the logical comparison of step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The logical comparison between בכור and מעשר שני
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: בכור has the extra strictness of blood and fats on the מזבח, which מעשר שני lacks

steps.title: The verse links tithe and firstborn
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק lists מעשר and בכור together. This היקש teaches that both are eaten only inside the walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק says: "And you shall eat before ה׳ your God... the tithe of your grain, your wine, and your oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and your flock." It puts מעשר side by side with בכור: just as בכור is eaten only inside the walls, מעשר is too.
steps.whatsHappening: Since logic failed, the ברייתא proves the rule from a פסוק instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A היקש comes straight from the פסוק, so it does not depend on the two items being equally strict. That is why the objection from step 11 no longer matters, and the eating rule of בכור carries over to מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: "The פסוק teaches": bringing a proof from the תורה
Compares two things because the פסוק places them together (היקש)
The tithe of your grain

steps.whatToRemember: מעשר שני is eaten only inside the walls of ירושלים. This is learned from a היקש to בכור, not from logic.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a היקש can work even when a logical comparison has been broken.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states:
“And you shall eat before the Lord your God…
the tithe of your grain, your wine, and your oil,
and the firstborn of your herd and your flock” —
it compares tithe to firstborn:

phrases.aramaic: מָה בְּכוֹר אֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל אֶלָּא לִפְנִים מִן הַחוֹמָה,
phrases.english: just as a firstborn is eaten only within the wall,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַעֲשֵׂר אֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל אֶלָּא לִפְנִים מִן הַחוֹמָה.
phrases.english: so too tithe is eaten only within the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected logic of step 11 with a proof from a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That מעשר שני is eaten only inside the walls
steps.raayaSupportSource: The היקש in דברים 14:23 between מעשר and בכור

steps.title: Why would anyone think otherwise?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what made בן עזאי think that מעשר שני could be eaten anywhere within sight of the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was bothering בן עזאי that made him say "you might think"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the "you might think" idea came from. It is setting up an explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יכול needs some real reason behind it. The גמרא wants to know what made the idea of eating anywhere within sight of the city seem possible at all.

keyTerms.meaning: "What was bothering him?": asking for the reason behind an idea

phrases.english: What was difficult for him
that he said “you might think”?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at the יכול of step 9 and asks for its basis.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason behind בן עזאי's "you might think"

steps.title: In שילה, מעשר שני was eaten anywhere within sight
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from a משנה: in שילה, קדשים קלים and מעשר שני were eaten anywhere within sight of it. In ירושלים they were eaten only inside the walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: You could say it is because we learned in a משנה: The only difference between שילה and ירושלים is that in שילה, קדשים קלים and מעשר שני are eaten anywhere it can be seen from, while in ירושלים they are eaten inside the wall. And likewise, קדשי קדשים are eaten inside the curtains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a משנה about שילה, where מעשר שני really was eaten anywhere within sight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the rule in שילה was "anywhere within sight," someone might think the same rule applies in ירושלים. That is where the idea in step 9 comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the משכן stood before the בית המקדש
Offerings of lesser holiness, like a שלמים
Offerings of the highest holiness
The curtains around the courtyard of the משכן

steps.confusionAlert: The "anywhere within sight" rule was true only in שילה. The משנה is the source of the mistaken idea, not the final halacha for ירושלים.

phrases.english: You may say: since we learned in a mishna:
The difference between Shiloh and Jerusalem
is only that in Shiloh one eats offerings of lesser sanctity
and second tithe in any place that sees [it],
while in Jerusalem, only within the wall;

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים,
phrases.english: and likewise, offerings of the most sacred order are eaten within the hangings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה about שילה, where מעשר שני was eaten anywhere within sight, could lead someone to think ירושלים works the same way.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches that ירושלים is different
steps.stepSummary: Someone might have thought ירושלים follows the rule of שילה. The היקש teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that in ירושלים too, מעשר שני may be eaten anywhere within sight. So the היקש teaches us that it may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the explanation: the mistake came from comparing to שילה, and the היקש rules it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of שילה, eating within sight of the city seemed possible. The היקש to בכור shows that in ירושלים, מעשר שני must be eaten inside the walls.

keyTerms.meaning: "You might have said": stating the mistaken idea
"It teaches us" that the idea is wrong

steps.whatToRemember: In שילה, מעשר שני was eaten anywhere within sight. In ירושלים it must be eaten inside the walls, as learned from the היקש to בכור.

phrases.english: You might have said

phrases.aramaic: בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם לַיְתֵי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בְּכׇל הָרוֹאֶה?
phrases.english: that in Jerusalem too one may bring second tithe [and eat it] anywhere that sees [the city]?
It teaches us [that this is not so].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from step 14 by linking it back to the היקש of step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The היקש is needed so that we do not apply the שילה rule to ירושלים. There, מעשר שני is eaten only inside the walls.

steps.title: Others raise a possibility: a בכור past its year might become פסול
steps.stepSummary: אחרים suggest a first thought: a בכור whose first year has passed might be treated like other disqualified קדשים and become פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: You might think a firstborn whose year has passed is like disqualified sacred animals, so it should become unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching from אחרים begins with a "you might think". This line sets up the question that the פסוק will answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many קדשים become פסול when their set time runs out. So one might think the same is true of a בכור, which should be eaten within its first year. The next step will reject this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: "Others": an unnamed תנא (or group) whose view is quoted in a ברייתא
"You might think": opens an idea that a פסוק will then reject
Whose (first) year has passed
Sacred animals that have become unfit

phrases.english: Others say: One might think
that a firstborn whose year has passed
is like disqualified sacred animals, and becomes unfit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the walls discussion, the גמרא brings another use of the same פסוק, this time from אחרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A first thought that a בכור past its year would become פסול.

steps.title: The היקש to מעשר shows a בכור does not become פסול
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק puts מעשר and בכור together. Second tithe does not become unfit from one year to the next, so a בכור doesn't either.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says "the tithe of your grain, your wine and your oil" and then the firstborn. It compares firstborn to tithe: just as tithe doesn't become unfit from one year to the next, so too a firstborn doesn't become unfit from one year to the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The פסוק answers the "you might think" from step 16. Because בכור is compared to מעשר שני, it does not become פסול when its year passes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחרים use the same היקש that the earlier תנאים used. רבי ישמעאל, רבי עקיבא and בן עזאי each used it for a different rule, but אחרים use it to teach about time. מעשר שני does not become פסול when a year passes, so the בכור that is compared to it does not either.

keyTerms.meaning: "The verse teaches": brings the פסוק that settles the question
"Compares": the פסוק sets two things side by side so they share a law (היקש)
From one year to the next

steps.whatToRemember: According to אחרים, the היקש of מעשר and בכור teaches that a בכור does not become פסול after its year.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"The tithe of your grain, your wine and your oil,"
phrases.notes: דברים 14:23. The פסוק goes on to mention the firstborn of your herd and flock.

phrases.english: it compares the firstborn to tithe;
just as tithe does not become unfit
from one year to the next,
so too the firstborn does not become unfit
from one year to the next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the possibility raised in step 16 using a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: A בכור is not פסול after its first year passes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The היקש of מעשר and בכור in דברים 14:23.

steps.title: Where do the רבנן learn this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן (רבי ישמעאל, רבי עקיבא and בן עזאי) already use the היקש for other rules. So where do they learn that a בכור is not פסול after a year?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, who use this פסוק for a different reason, where do they learn the rule about "from one year to the next"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the רבנן's source, since their היקש is already taken for another rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן here are רבי ישמעאל, רבי עקיבא and בן עזאי. Each of them already used the היקש of מעשר and בכור for a different rule (steps 1, 7 and 12). Since the היקש is taken, the גמרא needs another source for the time rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Who take it out for another reason: they use the פסוק for a different teaching
"From where do they know?": asks for the source

phrases.english: And according to the Rabbis,
who use it for a different reason,
phrases.notes: רבי ישמעאל, רבי עקיבא and בן עזאי each used this פסוק to teach a different rule (steps 1, 7 and 12).

phrases.english: from where do they learn "from one year to the next"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opposing side gets the rule from step 17 without the היקש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The רבנן's source that a בכור is not פסול after its year.

steps.title: The רבנן learn it from "שנה בשנה"
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn the rule from "תאכלנו שנה בשנה": "year by year" shows the בכור can carry over into the next year.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from "Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it year by year." This teaches that a firstborn does not become unfit from one year to the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's source: the words "שנה בשנה".
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Year by year" mentions two years. So the רבנן read it as saying the בכור is still fine to eat when the next year begins.

keyTerms.meaning: "They learn it from": introduces a source
"Year by year": read as covering two years
"Taught about": tells us what the פסוק comes to teach

phrases.english: They learn it from "Before ה׳ your God
you shall eat it year by year";
it teaches about the firstborn
that it does not become unfit from one year to the next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן learn it from "תאכלנו שנה בשנה" (דברים 15:20).

steps.title: What do אחרים learn from "שנה בשנה"?
steps.stepSummary: אחרים already get the rule from the היקש. So what do they do with the words "שנה בשנה"?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to אחרים, what do they learn from "Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it year by year"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around: if אחרים use the היקש, what is "שנה בשנה" teaching them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every word of a פסוק teaches something. Since אחרים don't need "שנה בשנה" for the time rule, it must teach them something else.

keyTerms.meaning: "What do they learn from it?": asks what a פסוק is used for

phrases.english: And according to the Others,
"Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it year by year":
what do they learn from it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving the רבנן a source, asks what the other side does with that same פסוק.

steps.title: "שנה בשנה" teaches that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night
steps.stepSummary: אחרים use "שנה בשנה" for a ברייתא: one day of this year and one day of the next. So a בכור is eaten for two days and the night between.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for what a ברייתא teaches: one day from this year and one day from another year. This teaches that the firstborn is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אחרים use "שנה בשנה" to teach how long a בכור may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Year by year" can describe eating on the last day of one year and the first day of the next. That shows a בכור is eaten for two days with one night between them. So both sides use "שנה בשנה", each for a different rule.

keyTerms.meaning: "He needs it for": the פסוק is used for a different teaching
For two days and one night: the time for eating a בכור

steps.whatToRemember: רבנן: "שנה בשנה" teaches a בכור is not פסול after its year. אחרים: the היקש teaches that, and "שנה בשנה" teaches it is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.confusionAlert: "One day of this year and one day of the next" does not mean you may eat it a year later. It means two days in a row that happen to cross from one year into the next.

phrases.english: They need it for what was taught in a ברייתא:
one day from this year,
and one day from another year;
it teaches about the firstborn
that it is eaten for two days and one night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20. This leads to the mirror question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אחרים use "שנה בשנה" to teach that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night.

steps.title: Where do the רבנן learn two days and one night?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן already used 'שנה בשנה' for a different lesson. So where do they get the rule that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: where do they learn that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around. אחרים used 'שנה בשנה' for the two-days rule, but the רבנן used those words for something else, so where do the רבנן get the two-days rule?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19 the רבנן used 'שנה בשנה' to teach that a בכור carries over into the next year. In step 21 we saw אחרים use the same words for two days and one night. That leaves the רבנן without a source for the two-days rule, so the גמרא asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: is eaten
for two days and one night (the eating time of a בכור)
from where do they know it?

phrases.english: And the רבנן,
phrases.notes: These are the חכמים who used 'שנה בשנה' to teach that a בכור carries into the next year (step 19).

phrases.english: that it is eaten for two days and one night,
from where do they know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, דְּנֶאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וָלָיְלָה אֶחָד מְנָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror question to step 20: now the רבנן need a source for the lesson אחרים took from 'שנה בשנה'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The רבנן's source for eating a בכור two days and one night.

steps.title: The רבנן learn it from 'like the breast of the waving'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the בכור 'shall be yours, like the breast of the waving'. From this the רבנן learn the two-days-and-one-night rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'It shall be yours, like the breast of the waving.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן have a different פסוק for the two-days rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בכור is compared to 'the breast of the waving', a part of a קרבן that is eaten for a set time. The same פסוק says 'it shall be yours' more than once, and that extra wording adds a day. So the רבנן get the two-days-and-one-night rule from here and do not need 'שנה בשנה' for it.

keyTerms.meaning: the breast of the waving: a part of a קרבן that is waved and given to the כהן

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a בכור is eaten for two days and one night. The רבנן learn it from 'כחזה התנופה'. אחרים learn it from 'שנה בשנה'.

phrases.english: The פסוק says:
"It shall be yours, like the breast of the waving."
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:18. The פסוק then repeats 'it shall be yours', and that repeat is what adds the extra day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: יִהְיֶה לָּךְ כַּחֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן learn the two-days-and-one-night rule from 'יהיה לך כחזה התנופה' in במדבר 18:18.

steps.title: Hadran: closing פרק אלו קדשים
steps.stepSummary: This is the closing line of the פרק called אלו קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק אלו קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק is finished. This line is the traditional goodbye to the פרק, saying we will come back to learn it again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new argument happens here. It just marks the end of the discussion about the בכור and the end of this פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: we will return to you (the closing words said at the end of a פרק)

phrases.english: We will return to you, "Elu Kodashim."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final answer in step 23.

steps.title: New פרק: sin offerings that are left to die
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists sin offerings (חטאות) that cannot be brought or redeemed and are left to die. It also says that some of these cannot make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The offspring of a חטאת, the substitute (תמורה) of a חטאת, and a חטאת whose owner died: they are left to die. A חטאת whose first year passed, or one that was lost and then found with a blemish: if this happened after the owner already got atonement with another animal, it is left to die, and it does not make a תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens. The משנה gives a list of חטאות that are not brought on the מזבח but are left to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is still a חטאת in category. But in these special cases it cannot be offered, so the rule is that it is set aside until it dies. The first three cases always die. For the later cases, the משנה adds a condition: if the owner already got atonement through a different animal, this one is left to die, and it cannot make a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה: marks the start of the משנה text
the offspring born to an animal set aside as a חטאת
an animal swapped in for a חטאת, which becomes holy too
they are left to die (locked away until they die)
its first year has passed (too old for a חטאת)
the owners have already gained atonement

steps.confusionAlert: 'Left to die' does not mean the animal stops being a חטאת. It is still holy. It just cannot be offered, so it is set aside until it dies.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list of חטאות that are left to die is the base for the whole new פרק, and the גמרא will analyze each case.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The offspring of a sin offering,
and the substitute for a sin offering,
and a sin offering whose owner has died,
they shall die.
phrases.notes: They are put away and left alone until they die. They are not offered and not redeemed.

phrases.english: And one whose year has passed,
and one that was lost and was found blemished,
if it was after the owner achieved atonement,
phrases.notes: He brought a different animal as his חטאת in its place.

phrases.english: it shall die,
and it does not make a substitute.
phrases.notes: If someone tries to swap a regular animal for it, the swapped animal does not become holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The offspring of a חטאת, the תמורה of a חטאת, and a חטאת whose owner died are left to die. A חטאת whose year passed, or one that was lost and found blemished, is left to die if the owner already got atonement, and it does not make a תמורה.
